findings.evidence: previous-version digest at dbff837f: "removed units (93, showing 40)". All 40 shown items have valid record rows (not-lost, intended-change, generic-model-knowledge drops, or user-accepted drops), but 53 removed units were not shown and could not be checked
findings.fix: Regenerate the digest with the full unit list (or judge against docs/audit/recovery/lesson-learned/sections.json in full) so every removed unit, including s014's lost 'Also worth noting' compact format, is checked against a row in docs/audit/recovery/lesson-learned/record.md

findings.evidence: "Rank them by observable consequence and evidence strength; a demonstrated trade-off beats a neat principle match." The removed 'lead with what works' rule is not replaced, so nothing says how to choose between a well-evidenced win and a well-evidenced introduced cost when both are candidates
findings.fix: Add one tie-break clause to step 2, e.g. "when a win and an introduced cost are equally evidenced, lead with the one the user's next change is most likely to repeat", which keeps the reflective purpose without restoring the dropped tone rules

findings.evidence: "Not for generic engineering tutorials, ordinary bug reviews, or implementing refactors." The near-misses in the skill's own trigger set (commit messages, release notes, postmortems, squashing history) are not named as boundaries, and the WHAT does not mention untracked files or pasted logs
findings.fix: Use when users ask what they learned, want an engineering takeaway, or reflect on recent commits, a branch diff, a specific commit, staged/unstaged or untracked changes, or a pasted git log, even without naming Git or a principle. Reads the changes and grounds one lesson in concrete code or test evidence, with a next-time practice. Not for generic engineering tutorials, bug reviews, refactor plans, commit messages, release notes or incident postmortems.

findings.evidence: Six evals cover casual, written, rename, range, untracked and no-change cases, but none tests the merge-commit gotcha (empty combined diff), the two-dot vs three-dot branch diff, or base-branch detection when origin/HEAD is missing
findings.fix: Add one eval with an evals/files/ fixture of a clean merge commit (git show output empty, --first-parent output non-empty), with assertions that the answer does not report 'no changes' and cites the first-parent diff

findings.evidence: Working changes row: "`git diff`, `git diff --cached`, and every `??` path from `git status`". `git status --short` collapses an untracked directory into one `?? dir/` line, so following this branch on a new untracked folder gives a directory path and not the new files in it
findings.fix: Change the row to "... and every `??` path from `git status --short --untracked-files=all` (the default collapses a new directory into one `?? dir/` line)", and add that fact to ## Git gotchas

findings.evidence: "On the base branch, a dirty tree means working changes first..." The skill never says how to tell whether HEAD is on the base branch, a feature branch or detached (e.g. checked out at a tag or in a rebase), so the default-scope branch has to be guessed
findings.fix: Add before the table: "Get the current branch with `git branch --show-current`; empty output means detached HEAD: treat it like the base-branch case (working changes, else last 5 commits) and say so."
